title: Implement verified-session handoff and rollover

requirement.summary: Implement ADR-0012 so a fresh verified session can be explicitly handed off without deleting identity and next can safely offer a separate rollover.

objective.rationale: The guided development loop needs an evidence-preserving terminal routing state before it can offer another admitted task.

goal: Add a versioned append-only handoff event, fresh-evidence preview and exact confirmation, Monitor separation, and deterministic zero/one/many-task rollover routing.
non_goals: Do not delete, archive, rename, or rewrite the current-task pointer, task contract, completion evidence, Monitor output, or prior events.
Do not make handoff mean requirement correctness, architecture approval, implementation acceptance, Monitor review, commit, merge, release, or deployment authorization.
Do not start the next task during handoff or silently choose among several admitted tasks.
Do not add update routing, background processing, telemetry, hooks, workflow changes, consumer migrations, or release behavior.
Do not commit, push, tag, publish, release, merge, deploy, or mutate an external system.
Preserve all earlier uncommitted bounded slices and report their combined working-copy scope honestly.
acceptance_signals: Event version 1.2 adds only the session.handed_off/handed_off pair while older 1.0 and 1.1 events remain readable and unsupported future versions fail closed.
govern handoff --dry-run is read-only and names the exact task digest, verified evidence reference, retained pointer, and one event target.

The write path requires exact HANDOFF from an interactive terminal and rechecks the exact task, latest verified completion, evidence freshness, full Git snapshot, and scope before one exclusive append.
Redirected, cancelled, stale, drifted, malformed, unsupported-progress, and preview-race paths write no handoff event; a matching prior handoff is idempotent.
The pointer and all prior artifacts remain byte-identical, and every handoff authority flag is false.
Monitor versioning displays handoff separately from verified completion and remains a read model that cannot claim human review.

After handoff, next excludes the exact handed-off digest and emits a replace-active dry-run command for exactly one other task, a TASK_JSON placeholder for several, or compact-task placeholders for none.
A changed digest is admitted only through the existing start replacement preview and exact REPLACE confirmation.
Schemas, CLI help, source documentation, and fixture tests change together, with no update, workflow, release, consumer, or external behavior change.
validation_commands: python -m unittest tests.test_development_handoff tests.test_event_store tests.test_development_session tests.test_next_action tests.test_development_monitor tests.test_development_event_export tests.test_user_documentation -v

items: A stale verified event could be handed off unless current evidence and every Git snapshot layer are rechecked.
A schema bump could make older local or exported events unreadable.
Concurrent confirmation could append duplicate handoffs unless the event target is stable and exclusive.
Rollover discovery could restart the same digest or conceal a human task choice.

stop_conditions: Stop if implementation requires mutating or deleting the session pointer, prior evidence, prior events, or task contract.
Stop if freshness cannot be re-established without appending a new completion event or trusting an assertion.
Stop if idempotence requires a multi-file transaction or overwrite behavior.
Stop if the command would imply semantic approval or choose a next task on the human's behalf.
Stop if compatibility requires silently ignoring an unsupported event version.

decision.rationale: The user explicitly asked to continue with the separately identified ADR-0012 implementation slice. The delivered task was paused on 2026-08-05 to remove it from automatic discovery; this is routing hygiene, not a claim of semantic completion, acceptance, merge, or release.
